title: Number Of Corner Rectangles
summary: Given an m x n matrix of binary values, count the number of rectangles formed by four distinct 1's at the corners.
statement: Given an m x n matrix of binary values, count the number of rectangles formed by four distinct 1's at the corners. Each rectangle must have its corners as 1's and no two corners can be the same.
constraints: Grid contains zeros and ones with at most 200 rows and columns.
Count axis-aligned rectangles whose four corner cells are one.
hints: Each rectangle is completed when a row repeats a pair of one-columns seen in an earlier row.
Count how often every column pair has appeared.
For each row’s one-column pairs, add prior count then increment it.
Every rectangle has one unique bottom row and column pair, so it is counted exactly when that bottom pair is processed.
editorial: Every rectangle has one unique bottom row and column pair, so it is counted exactly when that bottom pair is processed.

tests.explanation: Only rows two and four share two one-columns, producing one rectangle.
Three row pairs and three column pairs produce nine rectangles.
